Given:

At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

The spring constant, k, equals 56.4 kN/m. The side length of the block is side = 68.7 mm. W_f = 0.0713 kJ (the magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch). K1 = 511 J (the kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp). P_air = 98.7 kPa (the air pressure in the room). Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

What is the maximum compression of the spring, x? Give your answer in mm. In <steps>, report the intermediate values K2.
problem.target_desc: maximum compression of the spring

givens.desc: kinetic energy of the block at the bottom of the ramp
magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch

completion:
SI values: K1 = 511 J; W_f = 0.0713 kJ = 71.3 J; k = 56.4 kN/m = 5.64e+04 N/m.
Not needed: P_air, side.
K2 = K1 - W_f = 511 - 71.3 = 439.7 J
x = sqrt(2)*sqrt(K2)/sqrt(k) = sqrt(2)*sqrt(439.7)/sqrt(5.64e+04) = 0.1212 m
In mm: x = 121.2 mm
<steps>
